outcomes: In a Pants repository, each directory that holds first-party targets is a component, named by its directory, without a Putnami file
When the CI ran pants peek :: > pants-graph.json, the dependencies Pants infers from imports are the edges, so a change to a shared library marks the code that imports it as dependent
Without the export, observe still lists the target directories, says how to produce the export, and never runs pants
The JUnit and coverage reports pants test writes under dist/ land on the components that hold the tests and the covered files, and a bump in a Python resolve lockfile is a dependency change
nonGoals: Running pants, pex or any Python tool, or reading the Pants cache
Parsing BUILD files beyond the names of the targets they declare: the export carries the targets, their sources and their dependencies
Components finer than a directory, such as one per Pants target, and edges between targets of one directory
Lockfiles of resolves other than [python.resolves], such as JVM or Go resolves
Serving the detector over the workspace probe wire or from its own extension: it lives in @putnami/observe

requirements.text: A repository whose root holds pants.toml is a Pants repository. When the root holds pants-graph.json, or the file --pants-graph names, and it is a JSON array of target entries that each name an address, each target belongs to the BUILD file directory of its address or of its generator: src/python/pricing:lib and src/python/pricing/pricing.py:lib are one component src/python/pricing, of source orchestrator and ecosystem pants; // is the root. Any other file is a warning, and the BUILD files answer instead.

A third-party target, of type python_requirement, python_requirements, poetry_requirements, pipenv_requirements, pants_requirements, go_mod, go_third_party_package, jvm_artifact or node_third_party_package, and an internal target, whose type starts with _, make no component, with or without an export.

Each address in a target entry's dependencies, which Pants expands from the explicit and the inferred dependencies, is an edge from the target's component to the dependency's component, when the two differ. A dependency on a third-party or internal target, on an address outside the repository and on the component itself is no edge.

Without an export, each directory that holds a BUILD or BUILD.* file declaring a target other than a third-party or internal one is a component of source workspace and ecosystem pants, with no edge. The walk skips dist, node_modules, __pycache__ and hidden directories. An info diagnostic observe.pants_graph_missing names the export command pants peek :: > pants-graph.json and the path it read.

--pants-graph names the export, resolved against the invocation directory; without it the detector reads pants-graph.json at the repository root. The flag is declared in the extension manifest and needs a value.

Each lockfile the [python.resolves] table of pants.toml names, relative to the repository root, is a lockfile of ecosystem pypi. It is read in the PEX JSON lock format after its // comment header: each locked requirement of each locked resolve gives its project name, normalized as PyPI does, and its version. A lockfile that does not parse is the observe.lockfile_unreadable warning of the change analyses.

On a Pants repository with src/python/pricing, src/python/api importing pricing, and src/python/web, where a change edits pricing and bumps a package in the python-default resolve, the export gives the three components and the inferred edge from api to pricing, and marks api dependent; the JUnit reports under dist/test/reports and the coverage.xml under dist/coverage land on the components, with no unattributed case and no unmapped file; and the bump is a pypi dependency change.
On the same repository without the export, the analyses list the three components with no edge, so api is unaffected, and the observe.pants_graph_missing info diagnostic names the export command.
